input.label: SUPPORTED
input.change_reason: The initial verdict was INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE because the original evidence only showed that Bottling Investments contributed 3.1% of total operating income, which appeared positive. However, the newly retrieved evidence reveals critical information: Bottling Investments had an operating margin of only 7.4% in 2025 (E9), which is dramatically lower than the consolidated company operating margin of 28.7% and significantly lower than all other geographic segments (EMEA 39.7%, Latin America 59.1%, North America 25.9%, Asia Pacific 38.3%). This substantial margin differential - where Bottling Investments operates at less than one-third the consolidated margin - definitively establishes that the segment is a drag on overall profitability. When a segment has materially lower margins than the company average, it mathematically pulls down (drags) the overall profitability metrics, which is precisely what the claim asserts.

Our Bottling Investments operating segment is composed of our consolidated bottling operations, regardless of the geographic location of the bottler. Our consolidated bottling operations derive the majority of their revenues from the manufacture and sale of finished beverages. Generally, finished product operations generate higher net operating revenues but lower gross profit margins than concentrate operations.
